title: A fast implementation of the Monster group
abstract:
Let $\mathbb{M}$ be the Monster group, which is the largest sporadic finite simple group, and has first been constructed in 1982 by Griess. In 1985 Conway has constructed a 196884-dimensional rational epresentation $Ï$ of $\mathbb{M}$ with matrix entries in $\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1}{2}]$. We describe a new and very fast algorithm for performing the group operation in $\mathbb{M}$.
  For an odd integer $p > 1$ let $Ï_p$ be the representation $Ï$ with matrix entries taken modulo $p$. We use a generating set $Î$ of $\mathbb{M}$, such that the operation of a generator in $Î$ on an element of $Ï_p$ can easily be computed.
  We construct a triple $(v_1, v^+, v^-)$ of elements of the module $Ï_{15}$, such that an unknown $g \in \mathbb{M}$ can be effectively computed as a word in $Î$ from the images $(v_1 g, v^+ g, v^- g)$.
  Our new algorithm based on this idea multiplies two random elements of $\mathbb{M}$ in less than 30~milliseconds on a standard PC with an Intel i7-8750H CPU at 4 GHz. This is more than 100000 times faster than estimated by Wilson in 2013.
